text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- Austria's secret service intervened against the judicial charging of the murderers of three Kurdish leaders in 1989, as they said it could cause diplomatic trouble.

- The Finance Ministry's representative for the introduction of Europe's single currency Gustav Raab has stepped down from his post after discussions about a contract with the European Commission binding him only to propagate its opinion.
- Labour Union chief Fritz Verzetnitsch says the union's 'yes' to euro could easily become a 'no' should no job initiatives be started.
- Italy's Benetton group will take over motorway restaurant chain Wienerwald by the middle of May.
- Creditanstalt Leasing has founded a subsidiary in Budapest in a first step to expanding across eastern Europe.
- Flughafen Wien will raise its dividend to 16 schillings from 12 schillings even though profits fell in 1996.
- The government will have a special meeting on the 1997 budget this weekend. Chancellor Viktor Klima expects the budget to hold as long as the ministries stick to their budgets.

- Austria Tabak plans to start an exporting offensive in Asia, after the state-owned company, which is due to be privatised this autumn, reported a major jump in pre-tax profits to 1.77 billion schillings from 1.4 billion schillings.
- Motor engineer Steyr-Fahrzeugtechnik, a subsidiary of Steyr-Daimler-Puch, will build a 173-million-schilling development centre in southern Austria.
- Industry is worried about the union's move not to support European Economic and Monetary Union.
- Austria's telecommunications monopoly Post & Telekom Austria plans to raise prices for local calls while reducing the prices for long-distance calls ahead of the liberalisation of the market.
- The government plans to earn ten billion schillings from the privatisation of Austria Tabak. In a comparison of productivity among European cigarette makers the company is ranked third.
- Austria has lost three places in an international ranking of competitiveness and is currently rated 19th.
- Post & Telekom Austria plans to look for a new partner instead of postal savings bank PSK should an agreement on cooperation between the two not be signed.
